title: Map all requirement dimensions before starting analysis
when_to_use: When the task asks for strategies based on multiple dimensions (e.g., vehicle type, rating, time, location).
experience:
- **Explicitly list every dimension** mentioned in the task (vehicle type, service rating, time period, location, ride distance, payment method).
- **Create an analysis matrix** linking each dimension to the target metric (e.g., fare per km) before writing any code.
- **For each dimension, design a specific analysis** (e.g., hourly time bands, location clusters, distance bins) and ensure it is executed.
- **Check for joint analysis needs**—if the task implies combining dimensions (e.g., "which vehicle type during peak hours"), plan cross‑tabulations or interaction models.
- **After each analysis step, tick off the dimension** in a coverage ledger to avoid missing any.
checklist: List all explicit and implied dimensions
Verify all dimensions are covered before final report
common_failure_prevented: Missing multi-dimensional joint analysis (e.g., ignoring time, location, distance) that leads to incomplete strategies.

title: Execute time‑based segmentation before concluding
when_to_use: When the task involves earnings, demand, or performance over time (e.g., annual earnings, peak periods).
experience:
- **Extract time components** from datetime columns (hour, day of week, month, season).
- **Define relevant time segments** (peak vs off‑peak, weekday vs weekend, seasonal buckets).
- **Compute target metric per segment** (e.g., average fare per km by hour of day).
- **Identify optimal time windows** and quantify the uplift compared to baseline.
- **Include time‑based recommendations** in the final strategy (e.g., drive during 7–9 AM, avoid Sunday nights).
checklist: Parse datetime fields into granular components
Define time segments relevant to business
common_failure_prevented: Omitting time‑period analysis (e.g., no correlation between driving hour and fare) despite task mentioning annual earnings.

title: Analyze geographical and distance dimensions for operational strategy
when_to_use: When the task involves location‑based or distance‑based decisions (e.g., pickup/drop areas, short‑haul vs long‑haul).
experience:
- **Extract location features** (pickup/drop zones, urban/rural, high‑demand clusters).
- **Create distance bins** (e.g., short <5 km, medium 5–15 km, long >15 km) using ride‑distance column.
- **Compute metric per location/distance bin** (fare per km, cancellation rate, total earnings).
- **Combine location and distance** with other dimensions (vehicle type, time) to identify high‑yield combinations.
- **Provide actionable location/distance strategies** (e.g., prefer short trips in city center, avoid long trips with low‑rated vehicles).
checklist: Parse location columns into meaningful clusters
common_failure_prevented: Skipping location and distance analysis (e.g., no correlation between operating region or ride distance and fare) leading to incomplete optimization.
